transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because I keep getting stuck on these thoughts… like if I miss one setting, or one access rule, or don’t catch some warning sign, then someone could get hurt or lose everything. I know part of me can see that it’s not completely rational, but it feels like it’s on me, and I can’t really just move past it.
Do these thoughts make you feel anxious or worried about what might happen if you don’t address them?

Yes. It makes me very anxious. It’s like if I don’t deal with the thought, I’m leaving some setting or warning sign unchecked, and then if something bad happens, it would be on me. I know that probably sounds excessive, but in the moment I can’t just let it go.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly—like checking things, going over scenarios in your mind, or following certain rules—to try to reduce the anxiety these thoughts cause?

Yeah… I do. I check things a lot. Deployment plans, audit logs, locks… sometimes old messages too. I’ll go back through them more than once, and I count through steps in my head until it feels… safe, I guess.

There have been times I’ve stayed at the office for hours after everyone else left because stopping before it feels complete makes me panic.
How much do these checking behaviors and thoughts interfere with your daily life — like work, relationships, or other activities?

It’s… pretty bad, I guess. Work has taken a hit. I missed a major cloud migration deadline because I couldn’t finish signing off on decisions, and now my team sort of works around me instead of depending on me.

Outside work, I’ve stopped going to basketball and salsa nights. I just… don’t show up anymore. So I’m losing some of the routines and people that used to keep me grounded.
